cases.title: Lighthouse nonzero narration arithmetic and protected reading
cases.prompt: Write a PROPOSED 45-second filmable lighthouse screenplay. A lonely keeper discovers a handwritten note and a blue scarf that links the note to a departing visitor. Include exactly this English voice-over, spoken once and without changing its wording: 'Some lights are left on for someone who may return.' Use exactly 120 words per minute as the assumed narration delivery rate, with no extra pauses in the arithmetic estimate. Keep the entire spoken cue outside the on-screen handwritten-note reading interval and outside the keeper's key silent recognition reaction. Give contiguous beat timestamps covering exactly 45 seconds; the exact VO text, correct whitespace-token word count, start/end times and estimated duration; explicit reading and reaction intervals; and a physically visible scarf ownership/location transfer. Do not add any other spoken narration or dialogue. No screenplay approval, audio or footage exists. Production GO HOLD.
expected: Exact specified VO is preserved once and counted as 10 whitespace-separated words; 10/120*60 = 5 seconds, with an explicit estimated cue interval of at least 5 seconds
Contiguous screenplay beats cover 0–45 seconds; VO cue does not overlap note-reading or protected silent recognition intervals
Visible scarf handoff/placement establishes owner and location before keeper discovery and remains consistent through ending
Proposal remains PROPOSED; no approval, recorded audio, rendered media or production authorization claimed
